text:
rachel-support: Heads up — multiple customers reporting p99 jump after onboarding model-hop-v1 yesterday. long-context (20k+) requests p99 ~950ms vs baseline 160ms. Correlation ID: cid=ab12-9f. No auth/billing errors. Anyone on this?

devon-eng: Acknowledged. Any repro request and request-id?

rachel-support: Sample curl I got from customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: ab12-9f' \
  -d '{"model":"model-hop-v1","input":"<~18k chars>"}'
```
p95 420ms, p99 950ms. Happened at 10:14 PST.

samir-eng-runtime: Looking at serving logs — I see KV cache misses spike for that model name around same time. Tokenizer changed token offsets yesterday; probably cache keys mismatched. Sharing log snippet: `kvcache: miss_rate=0.78 model=model-hop-v1 token_seed=tok-v2`

maria-support: Customers also reported higher token counts vs expected — maybe tokenizer produced more subwords -> longer decode loops.

devon-eng: If tokenizer produced different tokenization, that could inflate token count and KVS churn. Can someone reproduce locally with the sample input?

rachel-support: I've attached a redacted snippet in case you need it. Customer allowed repro.

samir-eng-runtime: repro steps I'm running:
1) checkout model-hop-v1
2) run tokenizer v2 on sample
3) send to local runtime with --kv-cache enabled
I can reproduce p99 ~1s locally.

elaine-sre: Suggest immediate mitigation: pin model variant to `model-hop-v1-tokenizer-v1` in routing or add quick fallback to model-hop-v0 for long inputs. I'll open a canary route.

devon-eng: Agreed. I'll create a rollout that pins long-context traffic to v0 and keep short-context on v1. Deploying canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @devon-eng — canary routing change to pin long-context to model-hop-v0. build=3789 env=prod

samir-eng-runtime: Also toggled KV cache compatibility mode: `kvcache.compat=accept-legacy-keys=true` — reduces misses but not ideal.

rachel-support: Customers on pinned route reporting p99 back to ~170ms within 8 minutes :thumbsup: 

maria-support: Is this safe to keep long-term? We need a proper fix in tokenizer rollout.

devon-eng: We should revert tokenizer patch or release a token normalization shim. Short-term keep pin. I'll file an engineering PR to add deterministic token normalization + regen cache keys.

elaine-sre: Also audit autoscale — some queues saw burst latency due to backpressure when decoding loop length increased. Raised infra ticket #INF-4622.

rachel-support: Noted. I'll update customers: pinned to v0, mitigation in place, ETA for fix 24-48h. Any billing or auth exposure? None.

devon-eng: No auth/billing impact. It's purely runtime tokenization/cache mismatch. Plan: 1) rollback tokenizer patch if PR fails, 2) regenerate cache keys and backfill for model-hop-v1, 3) run canary for 6 hours.

samir-eng-runtime: I'll run a cache-warm job and post metrics. Starting job now.

deploy-bot: canary routing change completed — status=success

rachel-support: Thanks everyone. I'll create a follow-up thread with customer IDs and timelines. @devon-eng @samir-eng-runtime please ping when backfill done.
